forecast-period.text: A high pressure ridge over SA will move to the east early Friday, as a trough moves over the state during the day, followed by a strong cold front early Saturday. A high pressure system will then move across the state, behind the front, and merge with another high located to the southwest of WA on Sunday to extend a ridge across much of SA into next week. A low pressure system is also expected to move in vicinity of the WA border late Sunday and may extend a trough into far west SA into next week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Chance of early morning fog on and east of the ranges. Isolated to scattered showers in the west, extending over the Agricultural Areas and the south of the pastoral districts during the day. Thunderstorms are possible in western parts from the afternoon, extending into parts of the Eyre and Yorke Peninsulas from the evening. Maximum temperatures above average, tending near average in the southeast. Northeast to northwesterly winds freshening ahead of a west to southwesterly change extending from the west later.

Isolated showers about parts of the Agricultural Areas. Isolated showers developing in the far southwest, with the chance of a thunderstorm possible. Southeast to northeasterly winds, tending northwest to southwesterly winds about the Agricultural Areas.

Showers about the south of the pastoral districts, contracting east and clearing during the morning. Chance of a thunderstorm about the northern parts of the Spencer Gulf in the early morning. Showers about the Southern Agricultural Area, becoming isolated during the afternoon and mostly clearing by the evening. Thunderstorms possible about the South East districts until the afternoon, storms may be severe about the Lower South East with the risk of damaging wind gusts. Maximum temperatures below average, tending above average in the far northeast. Fresh to strong and gusty northwesterly winds about the Agricultural Areas, turning west to southwesterly during the morning and easing into the evening. Southwest to southeasterly winds extending over remaining areas, winds fresh and gusty about central and northern parts during the day.

Chance of patchy morning frost about the Flinders Ranges. Slight chance of isolated light showers about southern coastal districts. Isolated to scattered showers developing in the far west from the afternoon, with thunderstorms also possible. Maximum temperatures below average, tending above average in the northwest. Northeast to southeasterly winds, tending west to southwesterly in the southeast.

text.p: Chance of early morning fog about the ranges. Chance of isolated light showers about southern coastal districts during the day, with isolated to scattered showers and possible thunderstorms continuing in the west. Maximum temperatures below average. East to southeasterly winds, fresh and gusty about northern parts during the day, and tending southerly in the southeast.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Monday: 2 to 5 mm over the south of the pastoral districts, although local falls of 5 to 10 mm are possible. 5 to 10 mm in the far west and the Agricultural Areas, with local falls of 10 to 20 mm possible. Higher local falls of 15 to 25 mm are also possible about the Mount Lofty Ranges, Lower South East, and with thunderstorms.
